A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Riemannian generative decoder research. All 14 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including appendices, were readable. Textual and visual inspection supports matching retained, relocated and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on cell-cycle expression, synthetic branching diffusion and human mitochondrial DNA, including baseline comparisons and noise/curvature ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds downstream prediction, generative-fidelity discrimination, runtime measurements, held-out mitochondrial-DNA results and training-trajectory analysis.

M1.justification: The per-sample manifold latents, decoder, RiemannianAdam optimization and metric-scaled noise procedure remain. Replacing MLE terminology with MAP clarifies the already prior-containing objective. Newly documented initialization strategies do not establish that the underlying procedure changed.

E1.justification: The three datasets remain, but evaluation substantially expands beyond reconstruction and geometric correspondence. Section 4.4 and Appendices I–J add cell-generation discrimination, cell-stage classification, cyclic-phase regression, and mitochondrial-DNA classification of geographical region and two haplogroup resolutions.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–2 remain. v2 adds RGD with Lee and Park's explicit intrinsic-curvature penalty to runtime and alignment comparisons, includes a Euclidean ΔVAE timing variant, and evaluates P-VAE against RGD in mitochondrial-DNA downstream prediction.

E3.justification: New protocols include discriminator training/evaluation on separate halves of the cell-cycle test set, supervised latent-feature prediction, and full-gene timing at 5, 50 and 500 latent dimensions. Appendix C also revises baseline settings from approximate architectural matching and additional-parameter defaults to identical backbones with model/dataset-specific tuning. This reported revision does not establish that retained tables were rerun.

E4.justification: The original noise and curvature sweeps are retained. Appendix K adds a targeted analysis of distance-correlation trajectories during training with noise, without noise and with explicit curvature regularization. Table 4 additionally examines computational robustness as latent dimensionality increases.

E5.justification: Table 4 newly reports runtime means and standard deviations across 100 post-warmup epochs. Figure S5 specifies five runs for RGD conditions but one prematurely stopped explicit-regularizer run. Existing five-initialization and three-run reporting remains; the new utility and generative-fidelity tables report point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the earlier mitochondrial-DNA training entries retain their numerical values. Substantial new results appear in Tables 3–4, Tables S1–S3 and Figure S5. For example, new rCRS region-classification XGB accuracies are 0.97 for regularized hyperbolic RGD, 0.85 for Euclidean RGD and 0.65 for P-VAE. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 adds parameter priors to the formal background MAP objective, and Section 2.2 introduces the mathematical expression for Lee and Park's explicit curvature penalty. The proposed noise regularizer and curvature-versus-noise derivation remain substantively the same; their expanded presentation does not constitute a new proof.

C1.justification: The encoderless, any-manifold representation-learning claim remains. However, v2's contribution list and conclusion substantially extend the main claims to high-dimensional scalability and numerical stability relative to variational alternatives, together with broader predictive and generative utility. Higher-dimensional scaling was presented principally as future work in v1.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new training trajectories as evidence that noise helps internalize the prescribed geometry, and qualifies utility/generation evaluations as sanity checks. It removes v1's explicit warning that optimized test latents favor RGD reconstruction comparisons and its detailed cross-study benchmarking caveats. The limitation of memory growing with dataset size remains.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents training initialization and selection among test-time starting points. Section 4.4 specifies the timing experiment's CPU allocation and decoder layers, and a reproducibility statement describes configurations and scripts. Existing general hyperparameters and hardware are retained. Appendix A also introduces an inconsistent argument order between the noise-function call and definition.

R1.justification: v2 adds Huang et al. (2022) to the dimensionality-reduction motivation and Lee and Park (2023) as a substantive curvature-regularization comparison. It contrasts their explicit derivative-based penalties with its noise-induced regularization. The broader related-work coverage and relationship to the Deep Generative Decoder remain.

P1.justification: v2 adds an explicit contribution list and reproducibility/LLM statements, clarifies MAP terminology and optimization, and condenses several results discussions. Appendices are expanded and reorganized, but the main Background–Methodology–Results sequence and substantial existing exposition remain.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive resizing and repositioning of displays; Figure 2 changes from a 2-by-2 arrangement to one row. The old Table 3 becomes expanded Table S1, and the duplicated mutation histogram remains only as Figure S1. New utility/runtime tables and Figure S5 substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of practical usefulness and computational feasibility, which v1 left largely untested. Held-out mitochondrial-DNA results, downstream prediction, high-dimensional timing and the regularizer comparison provide evidence beyond low-dimensional visualizations and reconstruction correlations. Removing the test-time comparison caveat is a regression, and uncertainty reporting for new utility results is limited, but the added evidence addresses important validation gaps and yields a substantial net improvement.
